searches.note: Twenty six searches of a share of twenty eight, none of them the author's; two left unspent. One was restricted to the house's and its importers' domains (cletochiarli.com, lambruscovalley.it, dallaterra.com) and one to the house's and the press's (zerbina.com, gazzettadiparma.it, fleetstreetwine.com, bibenda.it), read as primary where the summary drew on the house. Eight more blocked the author's own sources so that a second, independent source would show: chiarli.it and Bottle of Italy, medici.it, Gambero Rosso International and Kobrand, cantinapaltrinieri.it, Primal Wine and Decanter, zerbina.com and Vinodabere, lastoppa.it, Louis Dressner, Bowler Wine and Decanter. One went to the Sorbara disciplinare and its decree, one to the DOCG of Albana, one to Riunite, one to Sorbara's colour and its flowers, one to the stress of Ermete. No WebFetch was tried. Every record was tested; no fact that rests on no source was kept in a record marked checked.

method: Each record was read with one instruction, refute it: the founding year, the people and their dates, the classification and its year, the grapes, the sites, the making and its months, the drinking window, the serving temperature, the label words, every beat of the story, the others, the traps, the cards and the questions; then the house rules (nobody living named, no price, no score, nothing volatile, no judging superlative, no bare family word, British spelling, no dash).

The searches went first to sources the author did not cite, with the author's domains blocked, for the second source of each date, person and place; then to the appellations' texts (the Lambrusco di Sorbara disciplinare and decree, the DOCG of Albana) and to the house's own pages where only the house could say.

Where a detail rested on no source the refuter read (the inn's rooms, the Paris bottle, the narrowest strip, Albana's thick skins, the litres of Zerbina's tanks, west of the Marzeno, the grapes of Marzieno, the Pinot Noir and Cabernet Sauvignon of La Stoppa's founder, a habit of the Piacenza hills, LaRiserva's 2013, Piria) it was cut or set as the sources give it; where the sources corrected the record (the names of Chiarli's Fondatore and Medici's I Quercioli, LaRiserva a spumante and no Riserva, Riunite in place of the large cooperatives, Ageno's blend, labels and casks) the record was set right with its source.

Prices, scores and ranks met in the results (merchants' prices, a 91 of a critic and a 90 of a guide for LaRiserva, Falstaff's 94 for AR, three glasses for Concerto and the Premium, Veronelli's best passito ever) were read and not used; hectares and bottles a year were left out.

tested: Founded 1860 and the inn: the results from Lambrusco Valley and Dalla Terra's producer page (Cleto Chiarli kept the Osteria dell'Artigliere in the old centre of Modena and in 1860 gave up the innkeeper's trade to make Lambrusco alone) and the Cleto Chiarli history page: confirmed. The library's 1860 holds; no source gives the founder's dates, so he is not named apart from the house.
The Mention Honorable at the Exposition Universelle of 1900: Lambrusco Valley, the Cleto Chiarli history and Dalla Terra's sheet: confirmed. The label term stands.

Vecchia Modena brought back in 1980 at the national congress of the oenologists (Assoenologi): the Cleto Chiarli history page, which names it Vecchia Modena Brut: confirmed as the house's account. That the name was dropped in the middle of the twentieth century rests on the house alone and is hedged as its account in the question.
The estate branch and the Premium: Tenute Agricole founded in 2000 by the house's account and a result on the Fondatore, in 2001 by Dalla Terra's presentation: hedged in the story.

The making in tank: Dalla Terra's sheet (Sorbara alone, Charmat method, grapes from Sozzigalli) beside the house's sheet: confirmed. The house's history also claims the first Charmat of Emilia-Romagna in 1959, a claim of a first on one source, left out.

Sozzigalli: about 25 to 30 hectares of Sorbara (left out as volatile), in Soliera by Dalla Terra and in Bomporto by the house's FAQ; the record names neither commune and keeps the house's own words for its soils.

The DOC: the disciplinare of 1992 and 1997 (Valoritalia's copy, the Gazzetta text) gives Sorbara at least 60 per cent and Salamino at most 40, and the amendments of 2024 keep it; the DOC dates from the decree of 1 May 1970: confirmed, the grapes, the label term and the first trap stand.

The pale trap: the Napa Valley Wine Academy and Wein-Plus give Sorbara's functionally female flowers, its poor set and its need of Salamino as a pollinator, and give it as the palest of the family; none ties the colour to the poor set, so the trap was rewritten.

The house's bottle refermented Sorbara: Superiore.de, Callmewine, Gambero Rosso and Dalla Terra name it Lambrusco (di Sorbara) del Fondatore, refermented in bottle by the ancestral method; wine.com says it is not disgorged and Dalla Terra speaks of disgorging, so its sediment is left out.

The house rules: no living person named (the house keeps its name; the founder is not named apart from it), no price, no score (the guide's top award left out as a rating), nothing volatile (hectares and bottles a year left out), no judging superlative (the reference reworded), British, no dash. The tank question has one key and four ways of making a sparkle; the year question's keys are the house's own dates, its explanation teaches each.

tested: Founded 1890 and the three taverns: an importer's or merchant's page among the results (Profile Wine Group, Winedering: Remigio Medici kept three taverns before founding a winery, his son Ermete enlarged it) and the house's history (its sons Valter and Giorgio began to export): confirmed as the house's account. The Strada dei Vini page says the founder set up a cellar at the start of the 1900s, and a blog on Ca' de' Medici gives 1911 for Remigio's firm and 1955 for Ermete's own company at Gaida; founded keeps the house's year and the matter is open.

The collapse and the fourth generation: the house's history (sales of the Emilian trade collapsed in 1988 under overproduction; the fourth generation joined that year, replanted and cut yields some 35 per cent below the rules): confirmed as the house's account, as the story hedges it.

Concerto of 1993, Lambrusco Salamino from Tenuta La Rampata: the house's history (in 1993 Concerto, a cru of Lambrusco Salamino, was born) and a merchant's result: confirmed. The claim of the first single vineyard Lambrusco stays out.

La Rampata at Montecchio Emilia in the Enza valley, a house of the 1800s with the acetaia: the Strada dei Vini e dei Sapori, Terre di Montechiarugolo and Corriere del Vino: confirmed. Gravel beside the clay: a result from the house and vino.com.

The making: tank fermented in stainless steel (the house's sheet, Superiore.de); one merchant speaks of a single long fermentation in tank rather than two, which the record's pressure tank covers either way.

The sweet Lambrusco of Reggio's cooperatives: Wikipedia on Riunite and the Politecnico di Milano's atlas (the cooperative of 1950, the first cases in America in 1967, the boom of the 1970s): the sentence was set on Riunite.

Granconcerto and I Quercioli: xtrawine, vino.com and Vessel Liquor for a metodo classico Brut Rosso of Salamino (VSQ on one listing, Reggiano DOC on another); Kobrand and wine.com for I Quercioli Reggiano Lambrusco Secco of Salamino and Marani.
The respelling: Ermete is the Italian Hermes, stressed on its first syllable; no result gave the stress in words, so it is open for a dictionary.

The house rules: no living person named (the founder and his son described, the house keeping the son's name), no price (merchants' prices read and not used), no score (three glasses read and not used), nothing volatile (80 hectares and seventy countries left out), no judging superlative, British, no dash. The colour question has one key and four reasons; the taverns question has four callings and teaches the house's account.

tested: The founder: the results from Primal Wine, Barberry Garden and Le Caveau (a lawyer named Ageno in the late nineteenth century, who planted international varieties pulled out from the mid 1990s): confirmed; his first name is Giancarlo or Gian Marco, and no source gives his dates, so he stays described and founded stays empty.
The Pantaleoni purchase of 1973 and the daughter: the same results (bought in 1973; the daughter took over in 1991 after her father's death in one account): confirmed as written (in the 1990s).
Rivergaro and the Val Trebbiola: Agriturismo.it (Ancarano, Rivergaro), Callmewine and the house's pages (in the Val Trebbiola, not far from the Trebbia): confirmed.
Ageno first made in 2002: Delectable (first production 2002) and a review of the 2004 that calls it the third vintage, beside the house: confirmed.

The making: La Vite Turchese, More Natural Wine and Barberry (about four months on the skins in steel or cement, native yeasts, 40 hectolitre Slavonian botti for at least a year, at least two years in bottle, released when ready and out of order), and a note of the 2011 with a month on the skins: confirmed and filled in.

The blend and the label: a note of the 2011 (about 60 per cent Malvasia with Ortrugo and Trebbiano), More Natural Wine (Malvasia alone from 2017), Empire Wine (Vino Bianco 2016) and Leon and Son (Emilia IGT 2019): corrected.

Macchiona and Trebbiolo: the house's Macchiona page (the farmhouse among the vines), the merchants (old vine Barbera and Bonarda, Slavonian botti), Bowler Wine and xtrawine (Trebbiolo of Barbera and Bonarda): confirmed.

The house rules: nobody living named (the family's daughter and the cellar master unnamed), no price, no score, nothing volatile (32 to 58 hectares and bottles a year left out), no judging superlative (the orange wine of Emilia reworded), British, no dash. The tannin question has one key and four causes, its near miss the barrique answered; the replanting question teaches the order of the French and local vines.

No living person is named in the fragment; the lint's people check passes.
swapNote: The author proposed no swap, and the refuter proposes none. All five picks stand: Cleto Chiarli and Fattoria Zerbina are the library's; Medici Ermete, Paltrinieri and La Stoppa are real houses of their appellations, each making the wine the record tells, which their own pages and two or more independent sources bear out. Some importers call La Stoppa's Macchiona its flagship red; Ageno stays the wine the house is known by abroad, as the author left it.
planNotes: chiarli: the note is answered: the label is Vecchia Modena Premium, later ones adding Mention Honorable, Lambrusco di Sorbara DOC, made in tank by the Charmat method (the house's sheet and Dalla Terra's). Dalla Terra speaks of a Vecchia Modena Nero from the 2023 vintage, which the integrator may want to know.

medici-ermete: the note is answered: the house dates itself to 1890 (a sister house's history and the Strada dei Vini differ, open in the record), Concerto is Lambrusco Salamino of La Rampata first made in 1993, and every claim of a first is left out.

paltrinieri: the note is answered for 1926 (Enoteca Nederland, with Polaner on the generations); the note's Leclisse from the oldest vines is in no source of the refuter's, and Botrytis Enoteca puts Radice itself on the old vines of the Cristo, so the read-together agent may drop the words.

zerbina: the note is answered: 1966 (the house, the Gazzetta di Parma, Bibenda), Scacco Matto first made in 1987 (Bibenda, the house), the label Romagna Albana Passito DOCG, Albana di Romagna Passito on older bottles (Italian Wine Central for the name of 2011).

la-stoppa: the note is answered in part: Rivergaro in the Val Trebbiola is confirmed; the founder is a lawyer of the late nineteenth century with no dates in any source, so founded is empty and he is described; the label is Emilia IGT or Vino Bianco by vintage. The why's Malvasia with Ortrugo and Trebbiano holds for the earlier vintages only, Malvasia alone in later ones, so the why wants a word for the read-together agent.
